primitives.name: Factorial State-Space Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model The paper proposes a factorial state-space model (fSSM) for N players and K matches at irregularly spaced times t_k (Section 2): player skills evolve independently a priori as Markovian continuous-time processes, and each match outcome depends only on the two participants' current skills.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N': 'number of players', 'K': 'number of matches', 't_k': 'irregular time points', 'x^i': 'skill vector of player i'}
primitives.assumptions: Skills evolve independently as continuous-time Markov processes; match outcomes depend only on current skills.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When match sparsity is not exploited, computational cost scales linearly with N and K.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's team-rating state transition graph where each node represents a player's skill vector at time t_k, updated via match events.
layer2.telemetry: Skill variance over time and match outcome prediction accuracy.

primitives.name: Bivariate Poisson Attack/Defence SSM
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — import the factorial SSM framework with match-sparsity reduction, the discrete fHMM eigenmachinery (O(S2) updates via analytic eigendecomposition), the bivariate Poisson attack/defence SSM, and the EM parameter-estimation workflow into GSE's team-rating pipeline; do not re-derive Elo/Glicko/TrueSkill, which GSE already covers.

primitives.assumptions: Match scores follow a bivariate Poisson distribution with structured dependence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When goal counts exceed typical ranges, likelihood may become numerically unstable.

layer2.telemetry: Goal prediction accuracy and match outcome entropy.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in the factorial structure of the state-space model, which decouples player skill evolution while maintaining joint likelihood through sparse match-event tracking. This allows for scalable filtering and smoothing under O(N+K) complexity. The discrete factorial HMM eigenmachinery enables efficient computation of belief updates using spectral methods, avoiding costly matrix inversions. The bivariate Poisson attack/defence likelihood provides a principled way to model goal-scoring dynamics in team sports, capturing both offensive and defensive contributions. These primitives together support a unified framework for online rating, retrospective analysis, and parameter learning via EM. Failure modes include numerical instability in large state spaces and poor fit when match outcomes deviate significantly from Poisson assumptions.
